# Infinite vs Bretton AI for compliance operations


Bretton AI (bretton.com, formerly Greenlite AI) sells AI-native operations for the financial back office: agents layered over a bank's existing compliance systems and policies, plus a managed service that puts experts in the loop.[Infinite](https://infinite.net/) takes the other route: it runs its own compliance program on a network, with Compliance AI underneath and a named analyst signing every decision. The difference is not the audit trail. It is who owns the program and where the work compounds.


By[Nikhil Srinivasan](https://infinite.net/company/about) , Founder & CEO


·


Last updated Sep 14, 2026

TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Bretton AI describes agents that work inside your existing compliance systems, layered over your data and policies; the program, the stack, and the exam stay yours.
2. Bretton states every decision is logged with reasoning, evidence, and model version; per-decision logging is now table stakes across the category, not a differentiator.
3. Infinite runs its own live compliance program: the review gates and the evidence are structural, not configured into someone else's queue.
4. A counterparty cleared on Infinite is cleared for every business on the network; a program run in isolation cannot compound this way.
5. Infinite's guarantee is a property of the system, not of any model version, so it does not move when the models do.


01


## Two answers to the same math problem


Both companies start from the same observation. Review volume grows with the book, and review capacity grows with headcount, so a compliance program that scales by hiring is always a quarter behind. Bretton's answer is on its home page: "Grow the bank. Not the back office." Replace the labor in the queue with agents that work inside the systems the bank already runs.


Infinite's answer is to grow the program, not the queue. Run the compliance program once, on a network, so that the work done for one business is done for every business that transacts with the same counterparty. The queue gets smaller for everyone, not faster for one institution.


02


## What Bretton sells


As of September 14, 2026, bretton.com describes a platform with three parts (Templates, Builder, Workbench) and a category it calls Trust Infrastructure. Its agents are "audit ready agents that work inside of your existing compliance systems", "layered over your data and policies", with the Workbench as "the AI workspace where your team works every case alongside the agents". The audit posture is specific: "Every decision logged with reasoning, evidence, model version", and "production traces become eval sets".


In July 2026 Bretton launched a managed service. Its page frames the offer as "AI-native managed services" with "technology, not labor, at its core", consumption pricing, "onshore experts in the loop", and "named investigators on the judgment calls and on SAR-related work". It is a serious company with a serious product; its site lists regulated banks among its customers, and its thesis is clear: the BPO model is the thing to replace.


03


## Layered over your stack, or the stack itself


Here is the structural difference. On Bretton's model, your case system remains the system of record, your screening and identity vendors remain your vendors, your written policy remains the policy, and Bretton's agents and analysts work inside all of it. What improves is throughput in your queue. A counterparty cleared in your queue is not cleared in anyone else's, every provider still has to be procured and integrated, and the examiner's questions land on the same desk they always did.


On Infinite, the program is Infinite's own.[Compliance AI](https://infinite.net/compliance/ai) runs KYC, KYB, KYT, and AML work for every business on the network today: domain-tuned agents operate the real tools (screening, document verification, device intelligence, ledger history, the case file itself), draw on the context of the account graph, route every decision to a named human, and leave a complete, exportable trail. The account, the rails, and the compliance program ship as one system, which is why screening runs before funds move rather than beside them. And because the program is shared, a counterparty cleared once is cleared for every business on the network. First-time reviews that take around 30 days under one-off manual review close in 1–2 days.


> A vendor in your queue can make the queue faster. It does not make the queue smaller for anyone but you.


04


## The audit trail is table stakes now


Both systems log every step and keep a human on the decision, and a buyer should expect nothing less from anyone in this category. Two things are worth reading closely.


The first is whether the gate is structural, a question to put to any vendor: is the review step a setting, or a gate that cannot be turned off? On Infinite it is structural: every decision point routes to a named analyst and there is no configuration in which the AI approves, rejects, or closes a case. Four written boundaries hold: no decisions, no filings, no hidden actions, no policy changes.


The second is what the model version means. Bretton states it logs the model version on every decision, which is the right thing to do with a model you depend on. Infinite's position is that the exam posture should never be staked on a model version at all. Models improve and get replaced; the gates, the tools, the context, and the trail do not change when they do. The guarantee is a property of the system, not of any model in it.


05


## Managed service, or managed program


Bretton's managed service is a BPO replacement layered over your stack: its team and agents run your workflows in your systems under your policies. Infinite's[Managed Compliance](https://infinite.net/compliance/ai#managed-service) is the whole program run for you on the same system that runs Infinite's own, in one of three shapes: fully managed, co-operated, or self-operated by your analysts on Compliance AI. You keep the policy and the decision. The difference is that the program doing the work is a live one that clears every business on the network, not a deployment into your queue. Which shape fits is a conversation, not a checkout.


06


## When Bretton fits, and when Infinite does


If you are a regulated institution with an entrenched case system and vendor stack you intend to keep, and the job is capacity in that queue without headcount, Bretton's model is built for exactly that. If the job is operating a money product for business customers, where compliance and the money movement have to be one system, or you want the program run rather than the queue accelerated, that is the job Infinite is built for. For the wider landscape, see[case management AI: five models compared](https://infinite.net/learn/insights/case-management-ai) .


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### How is Infinite different from Bretton AI?


Bretton AI layers agents and a managed service over the compliance systems, data, and policies you already run; the program stays yours. Infinite runs its own compliance program on a network, with Compliance AI underneath: counterparties cleared once are cleared for every business on it, and first-time reviews that take around 30 days under manual review close in 1–2 days.


### Is Bretton AI the same company as Greenlite?


Yes. Bretton AI is the former Greenlite AI; the company announced the rename alongside its February 2026 Series B, and its positioning (AI-native operations for the financial back office) is the same company's. Infinite is not affiliated with either name.


### Does Infinite offer a managed compliance service like Bretton's?


Yes, in a different shape.[Managed Compliance](https://infinite.net/compliance/ai#managed-service) runs the whole program for you on the same system that runs Infinite's own, under your written policy, with your named analysts signing from the first case. It is a program run on a network rather than a service layered over your stack, and it comes fully managed, co-operated, or self-operated.


### Can we run Compliance AI over our existing case system instead of switching?


Yes. Institutions running their own program can point[Compliance AI](https://infinite.net/compliance/ai) at their existing case system, screening, and core; the system operates them as tools rather than replacing them. Nothing is re-underwritten to a different standard, and decisions stay with your named analysts under your policy. Talk to us about the shape.
